1	---
2	title: Project requirements
3	id: REQ-PROJECTS
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-04-20
7	related: [REQ-040, REQ-134, ADR-004, DES-040]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for projects: creation, slug and key uniqueness, plan
13	quota enforcement, the archive/restore lifecycle and its cascade onto issues, visibility, and
14	pagination of project listings. It does not define issue-level behavior (`issues.md`), though
15	several requirements here describe the boundary between the two — most notably the archive
16	cascade in `REQ-045`.
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	A project belongs to exactly one organization and is represented by
21	`src/server/db/schema/projects.ts`, read and written through
22	`src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts`. All business logic sits in
23	`src/server/services/project-service.ts`, which is the only caller of
24	`insertProject`/`updateProject`/`archiveProject`/`restoreProject` — the known exception is
25	the project settings page itself
26	(`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/page.tsx` is not on the
27	brief's layering-exception list, so it goes through the service like everything else in this
28	domain).
29	
30	Every project has both a `slug`, unique within its organization (unlike an organization slug,
31	which is unique globally), and a `key`, a short uppercase prefix — think `ENG` or `OPS` —
32	that is immutable once set and used to build human-readable issue identifiers like `ENG-142`
33	via `issueKey()` in `src/lib/format.ts`. The key is derived at creation time from the
34	project name by `projectKeyFromName` in the same slug/key namespace `uniqueSlug` occupies,
35	and once an issue exists under that key, changing it would silently break every previously
36	shared issue link, which is why `REQ-042` makes immutability a requirement rather than a
37	convenience.
38	
39	Archiving a project is a soft delete (`ADR-004`) with a deliberate cascade: `archiveProject`
40	in `project-service.ts` calls `issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject`, so a project
41	does not sit in an archived-but-still-fully-open state where its issues keep showing up in
42	cross-project issue lists. Restoring a project (`restoreProject`) does not attempt the
43	inverse cascade automatically — restored issues are a separate, explicit action — which is
44	why `REQ-047` is phrased as "without losing its issues" rather than "with automatic issue
45	restoration": the issues survive the round trip, but their archived state is not implicitly
46	reversed.
47	
48	Project quota enforcement is shared with the billing domain: `createProject` calls
49	`wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'projects', used)`, sourced from `billing-service.ts`'s reading of
50	`PLAN_LIMITS`, and the same quota counts archived projects (`REQ-044`) because an archived
51	project's data still occupies storage and still could be restored, so it would be
52	inconsistent to let it drop out of the count that limits how many projects an org can have.
53	
54	## Open questions
55	
56	1. `REQ-049` lets a project nominate a lead, but there is no dedicated permission action for
57	   "lead" beyond ordinary `member`/`admin` gating — whether a lead should get an ownership
58	   escalation analogous to issue authors (`REQ-026`) is unresolved.
59	2. `REQ-050`'s public-projects visibility is gated by the `public_projects` flag
60	   (`enterprise`-only), but there is no requirement here describing what an unauthenticated
61	   visitor to a public project can actually see, since Taskflow otherwise assumes every
62	   viewer is an authenticated member.
63	3. Whether `REQ-052`'s keyset pagination should expose a stable "jump to page N" affordance
64	   for very large project lists is a known UX gap, not a defined requirement.
65	
66	### REQ-040 — A project belongs to exactly one organization
67	
68	- **Priority:** must
69	- **Status:** implemented
70	- **Related:** REQ-001, REQ-010, DES-001
71	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `findProjectById`, `listProjects`
72	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
73	
74	Like every tenant-scoped entity, `projects` carries `org_id`, and every
75	`project-repository.ts` function takes `orgId` as its first argument. There is no concept of
76	a project shared between two organizations, and no project-level ACL beyond the org
77	membership and the project-membership narrowing described in `REQ-051`.
78	
79	**Acceptance criteria**
80	
81	1. `findProjectById` returns `null`, not another org's project, when the id exists but
82	   belongs to a different `orgId`.
83	2. `listProjects` never mixes rows from two organizations in one page.
84	3. A project's `org_id` is immutable after creation; there is no "move project to another
85	   org" operation.
86	
87	### REQ-041 — Project slugs are unique within an organization
88	
89	- **Priority:** must
90	- **Status:** implemented
91	- **Related:** REQ-002, ADR-008, REQ-052
92	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listTakenProjectSlugs`, `src/lib/slug.ts` — `uniqueSlug`, `assertValidSlug`
93	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`, `tests/lib/slug.test.ts`
94	
95	`listTakenProjectSlugs(orgId)` scopes the uniqueness check to one organization, unlike the
96	organization slug, which is unique globally. Two different organizations can both have a
97	project slugged `website`; the URL disambiguates by org slug first
98	(`/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/...`).
99	
100	**Acceptance criteria**
101	
102	1. `uniqueSlug` for a project only considers slugs already taken within the same `orgId`.
103	2. Two organizations may each have a project with an identical slug.
104	3. `assertValidSlug` rejects the same reserved-word and character-set violations it rejects
105	   for organization slugs.
106	
107	### REQ-042 — Project keys prefix issue identifiers and are immutable
108	
109	- **Priority:** must
110	- **Status:** implemented
111	- **Related:** REQ-061, REQ-076, DES-041
112	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `projectKeyFromName`, `src/lib/format.ts` — `issueKey`
113	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/format.test.ts`
114	
115	`projectKeyFromName` derives an uppercase key from the project name at creation. Once set,
116	no `updateProject` field allows changing `key`, because `issueKey(projectKey, issueNumber)`
117	in `src/lib/format.ts` is how every issue is displayed and referenced (`ENG-142`), and a key
118	change would orphan every link, bookmark and cross-reference already using the old prefix.
119	
120	**Acceptance criteria**
121	
122	1. `updateProjectSchema` does not accept a `key` field.
123	2. `projectKeyFromName` produces a key unique within the organization, resolving
124	   collisions the same way project slugs do.
125	3. `issueKey` output is stable for the lifetime of the issue's project.
126	
127	### REQ-043 — Project creation is subject to the plan's project quota
128	
129	- **Priority:** must
130	- **Status:** implemented
131	- **Related:** REQ-134, REQ-138, ADR-010
132	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`
133	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/contract/plan-limits.test.ts`
134	
135	`createProject` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'projects', used, 1)` before
136	`project-repository.ts#insertProject` runs. `free` allows 2 projects, `starter` 10, `growth`
137	100, `enterprise` unlimited (`Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`). A request that would exceed the
138	quota fails with `plan_limit_exceeded` before any row is written.
139	
140	**Acceptance criteria**
141	
142	1. Creating a project past the plan's `projects` limit returns `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a
143	   generic validation error.
144	2. The check happens before `insertProject`, so a rejected creation leaves no orphaned row.
145	3. `enterprise` orgs never hit this check because `wouldExceedLimit` short-circuits on the
146	   `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` sentinel.
147	
148	### REQ-044 — Archived projects still consume the project quota
149	
150	- **Priority:** must
151	- **Status:** implemented
152	- **Related:** REQ-043, REQ-046, DES-040
153	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `countProjects`, `src/server/services/billing-service.ts` — `checkLimit`
154	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
155	
156	`countProjects(orgId, scope?)` defaults to counting archived and live projects together for
157	the quota check specifically — the quota-relevant call site does not pass
158	`ArchiveScope: 'live'`. This is a deliberate choice: an archived project can be restored at
159	any time, and its stored data (issues, comments, attachments) does not disappear on archive,
160	so letting archived projects fall out of the quota would let an org accumulate unbounded
161	archived-but-restorable state on a plan sized for a much smaller working set.
162	
163	**Acceptance criteria**
164	
165	1. The project-quota check in `billing-service.ts#checkLimit` counts archived projects.
166	2. An org at its project limit with several archived projects cannot create a new one
167	   without first permanently deleting (`REQ-048`) one of them.
168	3. Restoring an archived project does not double-count against the quota, since it was
169	   already counted while archived.
170	
171	### REQ-045 — Archiving a project archives its open issues
172	
173	- **Priority:** must
174	- **Status:** implemented
175	- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-046, DES-040
176	
177	Because the cascade is destructive to other people's working views, `project:archive` is
178	gated at `owner` in `ROLE_MATRIX` — the same minimum as `project:delete`. An admin can
179	invite, remove and change roles, but cannot sweep a project's issues out from under the
180	team; that escalation was deliberate after the second time a departing admin archived an
181	active project on their last day.
182	
183	`archiveProject` in `project-service.ts` calls
184	`issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject(orgId, projectId)` in the same operation, so an
185	archived project never leaves open issues visible in cross-project issue lists or on other
186	members' boards. The cascade only touches issues that are not already archived; it is
187	idempotent with respect to already-archived issues.
188	
189	**Acceptance criteria**
190	
191	1. After `archiveProject` returns, `countIssues(orgId, projectId, 'live')` is 0.
192	2. `archiveIssuesForProject` returns the count of issues it archived, used for the
193	   `project.archived` event's summary.
194	3. Archiving a project with zero open issues succeeds without error.
195	
196	**Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`
197	**Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`
198	
199	### REQ-046 — Archived projects are hidden from default listings
200	
201	- **Priority:** must
202	- **Status:** implemented
203	- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-101, DES-001
204	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `shouldFilterArchived`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
205	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/soft-delete.test.ts`, `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
206	
207	`shouldFilterArchived(scope)` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` defaults `listProjects` to
208	`ArchiveScope: 'live'` unless the caller explicitly asks for archived rows, matching the same
209	pattern used for issues (`REQ-071`) and comments (`REQ-101`). This keeps every default view
210	— the project switcher, the dashboard, the settings project list — free of clutter from
211	projects nobody is actively using, while still leaving an explicit "show archived" toggle
212	available where it matters (project settings, the archive-restore flow).
213	
214	**Acceptance criteria**
215	
216	1. `listProjects` without an explicit scope excludes archived rows.
217	2. An explicit `ArchiveScope: 'archived'` or `'all'` request still returns archived
218	   projects, for the restore UI.
219	3. `getProject` by slug for an archived project still resolves by direct navigation, since
220	   hiding from listings is not the same as hiding from direct access.
221	
222	### REQ-047 — A project may be restored without losing its issues
223	
224	- **Priority:** must
225	- **Status:** implemented
226	- **Related:** REQ-045, ADR-004
227	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `restoreProject`, `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `restorePatch`
228	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`
229	
230	`restoreProject` clears the project's `archived_at` via `restorePatch()`. It does not touch
231	any issue row — the issues archived by `REQ-045`'s cascade remain archived until someone
232	restores each one individually, but their data (title, description, comments, labels,
233	attachments) was never deleted, only marked. "Losing its issues" here means data loss, which
234	soft delete structurally prevents; it does not mean the issues automatically reopen.
235	
236	**Acceptance criteria**
237	
238	1. `restoreProject` never issues a delete or a recreate; it only updates `archived_at`.
239	2. Every issue that existed before archiving still exists, with its full history, after
240	   restore.
241	3. `restoreProjectAction` requires `project:archive`'s permission scope in `can()` (the
242	   restore action reuses the archive-adjacent permission surface, not a separate one).
243	
244	### REQ-048 — Project deletion is permanent and owner-only
245	
246	- **Priority:** should
247	- **Status:** implemented
248	- **Related:** REQ-007, REQ-025, ADR-004
249	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/server/jobs/cleanup-archived-job.ts` — `runCleanupArchivedJob`
250	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
251	
252	Unlike `archiveProject`, there is no `deleteProject` in `project-service.ts` — permanent
253	project deletion in Taskflow happens only through the retention cleanup job
254	(`REQ-231`, `cleanup-archived-job.ts`), which purges rows archived past the plan's
255	`retentionDays`. There is no interactive "permanently delete this project right now" action
256	in the product; `project:delete`'s `owner`-minimum `ROLE_MATRIX` entry gates a capability
257	that exists for the retention pipeline's authorization model but is not exposed as an
258	Server Action today. This is flagged as a requirement because the permission entry exists
259	and is deliberately the strictest gate short of `org:delete`, even though the only caller of
260	that authority level is the scheduled job, not a person.
261	
262	**Acceptance criteria**
263	
264	1. `project:delete`'s `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `owner`.
265	2. No Server Action under `src/actions/projects/archive-project.ts`,
266	   `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/projects/restore-project.ts` or
267	   `src/actions/projects/update-project.ts` performs a hard delete.
268	3. The retention cleanup job is the only code path that permanently removes a project row.
269	
270	### REQ-049 — A project may nominate a lead
271	
272	- **Priority:** could
273	- **Status:** implemented
274	- **Related:** REQ-054, REQ-023
275	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
276	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
277	
278	`Project` carries an optional lead reference, set through `updateProject`. The lead is
279	informational within the current permission model — it drives display (whose name shows as
280	"Lead" on the project header) and is available to `project-settings-form.tsx` — without its
281	own dedicated `ROLE_MATRIX` action; lead-setting is gated by the same `project:update`
282	minimum (`member`) as any other project metadata edit.
283	
284	**Acceptance criteria**
285	
286	1. `updateProject` accepts a nullable lead field; clearing the lead is a valid update.
287	2. The lead must be a member of the same organization (though not necessarily of the
288	   project, since project membership is only enforced for private projects — `REQ-051`).
289	3. Removing a member does not force-clear projects where they were lead; the reference
290	   persists for historical display, consistent with `REQ-033`.
291	
292	### REQ-050 — Project visibility is private unless public projects are enabled
293	
294	- **Priority:** should
295	- **Status:** implemented
296	- **Related:** REQ-188, ADR-012
297	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts`
298	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
299	
300	`Project` has a `visibility` field, and the `public_projects` feature flag (`enterprise`
301	plan minimum, overridable) is what unlocks the ability to mark a project public rather than
302	`private`. On plans below `enterprise`, every project is effectively private regardless of
303	what the field says, because `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` is checked before the
304	visibility value is allowed to matter anywhere it is read.
305	
306	**Acceptance criteria**
307	
308	1. A `growth`-plan org cannot set a project's visibility to public.
309	2. `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` gates the visibility check, not merely the settings
310	   UI's ability to select the option.
311	3. Downgrading a plan below `enterprise` does not retroactively delete public projects, but
312	   does stop treating them as public for access purposes (see the note under `REQ-141`).
313	
314	### REQ-051 — Project membership narrows notification fan-out
315	
316	- **Priority:** should
317	- **Status:** implemented
318	- **Related:** REQ-111, DES-050
319	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` — `isProjectMember`, `listProjectMemberIds`
320	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
321	
322	`src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` holds explicit project membership
323	used for `private`-visibility projects. Notification fan-out (`REQ-111`) for a private
324	project's events is narrowed to its explicit project members rather than the whole
325	organization, so an admin invited into the org but not onto a sensitive private project does
326	not get flooded with notifications for work they cannot even open.
327	
328	**Acceptance criteria**
329	
330	1. `isProjectMember` gates fan-out narrowing only for `private` projects; public and
331	   organization-default projects fan out to the broader recipient set unaffected.
332	2. Adding a project member does not retroactively notify them of past events.
333	3. `listProjectMemberIds` is consulted before, not after, the notification payload is
334	   built, so a non-member never receives even a suppressed-content notification stub.
335	
336	### REQ-052 — Project listings are paginated by keyset cursor
337	
338	- **Priority:** must
339	- **Status:** implemented
340	- **Related:** ADR-008, REQ-078, REQ-179
341	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/base-repository.ts` — `encodeCursor`, `decodeCursor`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
342	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
343	
344	`listProjects` returns a `Page<Project>` built from a keyset cursor
345	(`base-repository.ts#encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor`), not an offset. `ADR-008` documents why:
346	offset pagination degrades on SQLite as the offset grows, and a keyset cursor stays stable
347	even while projects are being archived or created concurrently with someone paging through
348	the list.
349	
350	**Acceptance criteria**
351	
352	1. A project list page's `nextCursor` decodes to a valid `(id, sortValue)` pair via
353	   `decodeCursor`.
354	2. Requesting a page with an invalid or tampered cursor fails validation rather than
355	   silently returning page one.
356	3. Concurrent creation of a new project does not shift already-fetched pages' contents (no
357	   duplicate or skipped rows from an offset-drift bug).
358	
359	### REQ-053 — Project creation emits project.created
360	
361	- **Priority:** must
362	- **Status:** implemented
363	- **Related:** REQ-014, REQ-172, DES-060
364	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/lib/event-bus.ts` — `emit`
365	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/lib/event-bus.test.ts`
366	
367	`createProject` calls `emit('project.created', ...)` after `insertProject` succeeds. This is
368	what the search indexer (`REQ-172`) and the activity service (`REQ-220`) both react to
369	without `project-service.ts` needing to know either of those concerns exists — the
370	event-bus pattern (`ADR-005`) is what keeps project creation's responsibility narrow.
371	
372	**Acceptance criteria**
373	
374	1. `project.created`'s payload extends `EventEnvelope` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`)
375	   plus the created project's id.
376	2. The event fires only after the database write succeeds, never before or on failure.
377	3. A handler error in one subscriber (for example, search indexing) does not roll back the
378	   project creation or prevent other subscribers (activity) from running, per the event
379	   bus's isolation guarantee.
380	
381	### REQ-054 — Project settings expose per-project defaults
382	
383	- **Priority:** could
384	- **Status:** implemented
385	- **Related:** REQ-049, REQ-062
386	- **Implemented by:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
387	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
388	
389	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`
390	exposes the fields
391	`updateProject` accepts: name, description, lead, visibility (where the flag allows it) and
392	the archive action. These are project-level defaults distinct from organization-wide
393	settings (`REQ-005`) — a project cannot override which feature flags are on, only its own
394	metadata.
395	
396	**Acceptance criteria**
397	
398	1. Every field editable through `project-settings-form.tsx` round-trips through
399	   `updateProjectSchema` validation identically to a direct Server Action call.
400	2. The settings page renders the archive control only when `can(actor, 'project:archive')`
401	   is true.
402	3. Settings changes revalidate the project's cache tag (`projectTag(projectId)`) so the
403	   updated values appear immediately across the dashboard.
404

---
title: Project requirements
id: REQ-PROJECTS
status: approved
owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
last_updated: 2026-04-20

## Scope

This document defines the requirements for projects: creation, slug and key uniqueness, plan
quota enforcement, the archive/restore lifecycle and its cascade onto issues, visibility, and
pagination of project listings. It does not define issue-level behavior (`issues.md`), though
several requirements here describe the boundary between the two — most notably the archive
cascade in `REQ-045`.

## Context

A project belongs to exactly one organization and is represented by
`src/server/db/schema/projects.ts`, read and written through
`src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts`. All business logic sits in
`src/server/services/project-service.ts`, which is the only caller of
`insertProject`/`updateProject`/`archiveProject`/`restoreProject` — the known exception is
the project settings page itself
(`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/page.tsx` is not on the
brief's layering-exception list, so it goes through the service like everything else in this
domain).

Every project has both a `slug`, unique within its organization (unlike an organization slug,
which is unique globally), and a `key`, a short uppercase prefix — think `ENG` or `OPS` —
that is immutable once set and used to build human-readable issue identifiers like `ENG-142`

and once an issue exists under that key, changing it would silently break every previously

convenience.

Archiving a project is a soft delete (`ADR-004`) with a deliberate cascade: `archiveProject`
in `project-service.ts` calls `issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject`, so a project
does not sit in an archived-but-still-fully-open state where its issues keep showing up in

## Open questions

1. `REQ-049` lets a project nominate a lead, but there is no dedicated permission action for
   "lead" beyond ordinary `member`/`admin` gating — whether a lead should get an ownership
   escalation analogous to issue authors (`REQ-026`) is unresolved.
2. `REQ-050`'s public-projects visibility is gated by the `public_projects` flag
   (`enterprise`-only), but there is no requirement here describing what an unauthenticated
   visitor to a public project can actually see, since Taskflow otherwise assumes every
   viewer is an authenticated member.
3. Whether `REQ-052`'s keyset pagination should expose a stable "jump to page N" affordance
   for very large project lists is a known UX gap, not a defined requirement.

### REQ-040 — A project belongs to exactly one organization

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-001, REQ-010, DES-001
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `findProjectById`, `listProjects`
- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`

Like every tenant-scoped entity, `projects` carries `org_id`, and every
`project-repository.ts` function takes `orgId` as its first argument. There is no concept of
a project shared between two organizations, and no project-level ACL beyond the org
membership and the project-membership narrowing described in `REQ-051`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `findProjectById` returns `null`, not another org's project, when the id exists but
   belongs to a different `orgId`.
2. `listProjects` never mixes rows from two organizations in one page.
3. A project's `org_id` is immutable after creation; there is no "move project to another
   org" operation.

### REQ-041 — Project slugs are unique within an organization

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-002, ADR-008, REQ-052
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listTakenProjectSlugs`, `src/lib/slug.ts` — `uniqueSlug`, `assertValidSlug`
- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`, `tests/lib/slug.test.ts`

`listTakenProjectSlugs(orgId)` scopes the uniqueness check to one organization, unlike the
organization slug, which is unique globally. Two different organizations can both have a
project slugged `website`; the URL disambiguates by org slug first
(`/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/...`).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `uniqueSlug` for a project only considers slugs already taken within the same `orgId`.
2. Two organizations may each have a project with an identical slug.
3. `assertValidSlug` rejects the same reserved-word and character-set violations it rejects
   for organization slugs.

### REQ-042 — Project keys prefix issue identifiers and are immutable

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-061, REQ-076, DES-041
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `projectKeyFromName`, `src/lib/format.ts` — `issueKey`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/format.test.ts`

`projectKeyFromName` derives an uppercase key from the project name at creation. Once set,
no `updateProject` field allows changing `key`, because `issueKey(projectKey, issueNumber)`
in `src/lib/format.ts` is how every issue is displayed and referenced (`ENG-142`), and a key
change would orphan every link, bookmark and cross-reference already using the old prefix.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `updateProjectSchema` does not accept a `key` field.
2. `projectKeyFromName` produces a key unique within the organization, resolving
   collisions the same way project slugs do.
3. `issueKey` output is stable for the lifetime of the issue's project.

### REQ-043 — Project creation is subject to the plan's project quota

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-134, REQ-138, ADR-010
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/contract/plan-limits.test.ts`

`createProject` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'projects', used, 1)` before
`project-repository.ts#insertProject` runs. `free` allows 2 projects, `starter` 10, `growth`
100, `enterprise` unlimited (`Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`). A request that would exceed the
quota fails with `plan_limit_exceeded` before any row is written.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Creating a project past the plan's `projects` limit returns `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a
   generic validation error.
2. The check happens before `insertProject`, so a rejected creation leaves no orphaned row.
3. `enterprise` orgs never hit this check because `wouldExceedLimit` short-circuits on the
   `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` sentinel.

### REQ-044 — Archived projects still consume the project quota

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-043, REQ-046, DES-040
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `countProjects`, `src/server/services/billing-service.ts` — `checkLimit`
- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`

`countProjects(orgId, scope?)` defaults to counting archived and live projects together for
the quota check specifically — the quota-relevant call site does not pass
`ArchiveScope: 'live'`. This is a deliberate choice: an archived project can be restored at
any time, and its stored data (issues, comments, attachments) does not disappear on archive,
so letting archived projects fall out of the quota would let an org accumulate unbounded
archived-but-restorable state on a plan sized for a much smaller working set.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The project-quota check in `billing-service.ts#checkLimit` counts archived projects.
2. An org at its project limit with several archived projects cannot create a new one
   without first permanently deleting (`REQ-048`) one of them.
3. Restoring an archived project does not double-count against the quota, since it was
   already counted while archived.

### REQ-045 — Archiving a project archives its open issues

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-046, DES-040

Because the cascade is destructive to other people's working views, `project:archive` is
gated at `owner` in `ROLE_MATRIX` — the same minimum as `project:delete`. An admin can
invite, remove and change roles, but cannot sweep a project's issues out from under the
team; that escalation was deliberate after the second time a departing admin archived an
active project on their last day.

`archiveProject` in `project-service.ts` calls
`issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject(orgId, projectId)` in the same operation, so an
archived project never leaves open issues visible in cross-project issue lists or on other
members' boards. The cascade only touches issues that are not already archived; it is
idempotent with respect to already-archived issues.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. After `archiveProject` returns, `countIssues(orgId, projectId, 'live')` is 0.
2. `archiveIssuesForProject` returns the count of issues it archived, used for the
   `project.archived` event's summary.
3. Archiving a project with zero open issues succeeds without error.

**Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`

### REQ-046 — Archived projects are hidden from default listings

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-101, DES-001
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `shouldFilterArchived`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/soft-delete.test.ts`, `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`

`shouldFilterArchived(scope)` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` defaults `listProjects` to
`ArchiveScope: 'live'` unless the caller explicitly asks for archived rows, matching the same
pattern used for issues (`REQ-071`) and comments (`REQ-101`). This keeps every default view
— the project switcher, the dashboard, the settings project list — free of clutter from
projects nobody is actively using, while still leaving an explicit "show archived" toggle
available where it matters (project settings, the archive-restore flow).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `listProjects` without an explicit scope excludes archived rows.
2. An explicit `ArchiveScope: 'archived'` or `'all'` request still returns archived
   projects, for the restore UI.
3. `getProject` by slug for an archived project still resolves by direct navigation, since
   hiding from listings is not the same as hiding from direct access.

### REQ-047 — A project may be restored without losing its issues

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-045, ADR-004
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `restoreProject`, `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `restorePatch`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`

`restoreProject` clears the project's `archived_at` via `restorePatch()`. It does not touch
any issue row — the issues archived by `REQ-045`'s cascade remain archived until someone
restores each one individually, but their data (title, description, comments, labels,
attachments) was never deleted, only marked. "Losing its issues" here means data loss, which
soft delete structurally prevents; it does not mean the issues automatically reopen.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `restoreProject` never issues a delete or a recreate; it only updates `archived_at`.
2. Every issue that existed before archiving still exists, with its full history, after
   restore.
3. `restoreProjectAction` requires `project:archive`'s permission scope in `can()` (the
   restore action reuses the archive-adjacent permission surface, not a separate one).

### REQ-048 — Project deletion is permanent and owner-only

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-007, REQ-025, ADR-004
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/server/jobs/cleanup-archived-job.ts` — `runCleanupArchivedJob`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

Unlike `archiveProject`, there is no `deleteProject` in `project-service.ts` — permanent
project deletion in Taskflow happens only through the retention cleanup job
(`REQ-231`, `cleanup-archived-job.ts`), which purges rows archived past the plan's
`retentionDays`. There is no interactive "permanently delete this project right now" action
in the product; `project:delete`'s `owner`-minimum `ROLE_MATRIX` entry gates a capability
that exists for the retention pipeline's authorization model but is not exposed as an
Server Action today. This is flagged as a requirement because the permission entry exists
and is deliberately the strictest gate short of `org:delete`, even though the only caller of
that authority level is the scheduled job, not a person.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `project:delete`'s `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `owner`.
2. No Server Action under `src/actions/projects/archive-project.ts`,
   `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/projects/restore-project.ts` or
   `src/actions/projects/update-project.ts` performs a hard delete.
3. The retention cleanup job is the only code path that permanently removes a project row.

### REQ-049 — A project may nominate a lead

- **Priority:** could
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-054, REQ-023
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`Project` carries an optional lead reference, set through `updateProject`. The lead is
informational within the current permission model — it drives display (whose name shows as
"Lead" on the project header) and is available to `project-settings-form.tsx` — without its
own dedicated `ROLE_MATRIX` action; lead-setting is gated by the same `project:update`
minimum (`member`) as any other project metadata edit.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `updateProject` accepts a nullable lead field; clearing the lead is a valid update.
2. The lead must be a member of the same organization (though not necessarily of the
   project, since project membership is only enforced for private projects — `REQ-051`).
3. Removing a member does not force-clear projects where they were lead; the reference
   persists for historical display, consistent with `REQ-033`.

### REQ-050 — Project visibility is private unless public projects are enabled

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-188, ADR-012
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`Project` has a `visibility` field, and the `public_projects` feature flag (`enterprise`
plan minimum, overridable) is what unlocks the ability to mark a project public rather than
`private`. On plans below `enterprise`, every project is effectively private regardless of
what the field says, because `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` is checked before the
visibility value is allowed to matter anywhere it is read.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `growth`-plan org cannot set a project's visibility to public.
2. `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` gates the visibility check, not merely the settings
   UI's ability to select the option.
3. Downgrading a plan below `enterprise` does not retroactively delete public projects, but
   does stop treating them as public for access purposes (see the note under `REQ-141`).

### REQ-051 — Project membership narrows notification fan-out

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-111, DES-050
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` — `isProjectMember`, `listProjectMemberIds`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` holds explicit project membership
used for `private`-visibility projects. Notification fan-out (`REQ-111`) for a private
project's events is narrowed to its explicit project members rather than the whole
organization, so an admin invited into the org but not onto a sensitive private project does
not get flooded with notifications for work they cannot even open.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `isProjectMember` gates fan-out narrowing only for `private` projects; public and
   organization-default projects fan out to the broader recipient set unaffected.
2. Adding a project member does not retroactively notify them of past events.
3. `listProjectMemberIds` is consulted before, not after, the notification payload is
   built, so a non-member never receives even a suppressed-content notification stub.

### REQ-052 — Project listings are paginated by keyset cursor

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-008, REQ-078, REQ-179
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/base-repository.ts` — `encodeCursor`, `decodeCursor`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`

`listProjects` returns a `Page<Project>` built from a keyset cursor
(`base-repository.ts#encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor`), not an offset. `ADR-008` documents why:
offset pagination degrades on SQLite as the offset grows, and a keyset cursor stays stable
even while projects are being archived or created concurrently with someone paging through
the list.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A project list page's `nextCursor` decodes to a valid `(id, sortValue)` pair via
   `decodeCursor`.
2. Requesting a page with an invalid or tampered cursor fails validation rather than
   silently returning page one.
3. Concurrent creation of a new project does not shift already-fetched pages' contents (no
   duplicate or skipped rows from an offset-drift bug).

### REQ-053 — Project creation emits project.created

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-014, REQ-172, DES-060
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/lib/event-bus.ts` — `emit`
- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/lib/event-bus.test.ts`

`createProject` calls `emit('project.created', ...)` after `insertProject` succeeds. This is
what the search indexer (`REQ-172`) and the activity service (`REQ-220`) both react to
without `project-service.ts` needing to know either of those concerns exists — the
event-bus pattern (`ADR-005`) is what keeps project creation's responsibility narrow.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `project.created`'s payload extends `EventEnvelope` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`)
   plus the created project's id.
2. The event fires only after the database write succeeds, never before or on failure.
3. A handler error in one subscriber (for example, search indexing) does not roll back the
   project creation or prevent other subscribers (activity) from running, per the event
   bus's isolation guarantee.

### REQ-054 — Project settings expose per-project defaults

- **Priority:** could
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-049, REQ-062
- **Implemented by:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`
exposes the fields
`updateProject` accepts: name, description, lead, visibility (where the flag allows it) and
the archive action. These are project-level defaults distinct from organization-wide
settings (`REQ-005`) — a project cannot override which feature flags are on, only its own
metadata.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every field editable through `project-settings-form.tsx` round-trips through
   `updateProjectSchema` validation identically to a direct Server Action call.
2. The settings page renders the archive control only when `can(actor, 'project:archive')`
   is true.
3. Settings changes revalidate the project's cache tag (`projectTag(projectId)`) so the
   updated values appear immediately across the dashboard.

content.content:
1	---
2	title: Membership and roles requirements
3	id: REQ-MEMBERSHIP
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-05-11
7	related: [REQ-001, REQ-006, ADR-003, DES-011]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines how a user becomes a member of an organization, what the four roles
13	mean, how invitations work end to end, and the invariants that keep the last-owner rule and
14	authored-content ownership consistent under role changes and removals. It does not define
15	the tenant boundary itself (`organizations.md`) or what each permission action actually
16	gates on individual resources like issues and comments (`issues.md`,
17	`comments-and-mentions.md`), though the ownership-escalation mechanic is defined here because
18	it is a property of roles, not of any one resource.
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	Membership is a join between a global `User` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`,
23	the one repository that is not tenant-scoped) and an `Organization`, represented as a
24	`Member` row with a `role`. `src/server/services/member-service.ts` owns role changes and
25	removal; `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` owns the invite-and-accept lifecycle
26	that produces new members. Both call into `src/lib/permissions.ts`, which is the single
27	authorization entry point (`ADR-003`): `can()`, `assertCan()`, `explain()` and `canAll()`
28	all read from one `ROLE_MATRIX` table keyed by `PermissionAction`.
29	
30	The four roles — `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer` — form a strict total order captured
31	in `ROLE_RANK` (`src/types/member.ts`). `ROLE_MATRIX` records, for every action, the minimum
32	role required, and `hasRoleAtLeast` is the comparison every "at least this role" check
33	reduces to. The decision order documented in `permissions.ts` runs cross-tenant guard,
34	platform-staff bypass, role matrix, then ownership escalation — so a `member` who is not
35	the assignee of an issue is denied `issue:update` by the matrix, but the same `member` who
36	authored that issue is granted it by the escalation step that runs after the matrix would
37	otherwise deny.
38	
39	Invitations are their own short-lived entity (`src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts`),
40	keyed by a hash of the invite token rather than the plaintext token, so the unauthenticated
41	accept page (`src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`) never has to trust a value it cannot
42	verify against the database. `invitation-service.ts` checks the seat quota
43	(`wouldExceedLimit`) and the `member:invite` rate-limit bucket before it mints a token,
44	which is why an org near its seat limit gets `plan_limit_exceeded` before Taskflow ever
45	writes a pending invitation row it would have to clean up later.
46	
47	## Open questions
48	
49	1. `REQ-026`'s ownership escalation list (`issue:update`, `issue:archive`,
50	   `comment:update`, `comment:delete`, `notification:manage`) is fixed in `permissions.ts`;
51	   whether project leads (`REQ-049`) should get an analogous escalation for
52	   `project:update` is an open product question, not yet a requirement.
53	2. `REQ-027`'s platform-staff bypass has no requirement here describing how staff status is
54	   granted or revoked — that lives outside this corpus's scope (an internal admin tool).
55	3. `REQ-032` checks seats at invite time; whether an accepted invitation should re-check the
56	   seat quota at acceptance time (a window where the quota could have been exhausted by a
57	   concurrent invite) is unresolved — see the note under `REQ-030`.
58	
59	### REQ-020 — Four roles form a strict rank order
60	
61	- **Priority:** must
62	- **Status:** implemented
63	- **Related:** ADR-003, REQ-021, DES-011
64	- **Implemented by:** `src/types/member.ts` — `ROLE_RANK`, `hasRoleAtLeast`
65	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/schemas/member.schema.test.ts`
66	
67	`ROLE_RANK` in `src/types/member.ts` orders the four roles `owner > admin > member >
68	viewer`, and every "minimum role" check in the product — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `hasRoleAtLeast`,
69	the last-owner guard — is expressed against this single ordering rather than an ad hoc set
70	of role comparisons scattered per feature. There is no fifth role and no per-organization
71	custom role; Taskflow deliberately does not offer role customization, trading flexibility
72	for a permission surface simple enough to reason about in one file.
73	
74	**Acceptance criteria**
75	
76	1. `ROLE_RANK` assigns a strictly increasing numeric rank to `viewer < member < admin <
77	   owner`.
78	2. Every comparison of "is this role at least that role" in the codebase goes through
79	   `hasRoleAtLeast`, not a hand-rolled string comparison.
80	3. Role values outside the four are rejected at the schema layer (`src/schemas/role.ts`).
81	
82	### REQ-021 — Role rank determines the default permission decision
83	
84	- **Priority:** must
85	- **Status:** implemented
86	- **Related:** REQ-020, ADR-003, REQ-027
87	
88	For any `PermissionAction`, `ROLE_MATRIX` declares a minimum role; `can()` compares the
89	actor's role rank against that minimum after the cross-tenant and platform-staff checks have
90	already passed. This is the `granted_by_role` / `denied_by_role` branch of `explain()`'s
91	decision reasons, and it is the default path — most calls to `can()` in the app resolve here
92	without ever reaching the ownership-escalation step.
93	
94	**Acceptance criteria**
95	
96	1. `can(actor, action)` returns `true` whenever `actor.role` rank is greater than or equal
97	   to the action's `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum.
98	2. `explain()` reports `granted_by_role` or `denied_by_role` for every action not covered
99	   by an escalation.
100	3. `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` sweeps every action against every role.
101	
102	**Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts`
103	**Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
104	
105	### REQ-022 — Viewers have read-only access across the product
106	
107	- **Priority:** must
108	- **Status:** implemented
109	- **Related:** REQ-020, REQ-181, REQ-224
110	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/components/domain/permission/permission-gate.tsx`
111	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`
112	
113	`viewer` is the minimum role for every `*:read` action in `ROLE_MATRIX` —
114	`org:read`, `member:read`, `project:read`, `issue:read`, `comment:read`,
115	`notification:read` — and the minimum role for no mutating action at all. A viewer can open
116	every screen a member can, but every button that would write is hidden by
117	`PermissionGate` (see `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`) and, more importantly,
118	would be denied server-side even if a viewer forged the request.
119	
120	**Acceptance criteria**
121	
122	1. No `*:create`, `*:update`, `*:delete`, `*:archive` or `*:manage_*` action's `ROLE_MATRIX`
123	   minimum is `viewer`.
124	2. Every `*:read` action's minimum is `viewer` or lower (there is no lower role).
125	3. A viewer's forged Server Action call is denied server-side regardless of what the client
126	   rendered.
127	
128	### REQ-023 — Members may create and edit issues, projects and comments
129	
130	- **Priority:** must
131	- **Status:** implemented
132	- **Related:** REQ-060, REQ-090, REQ-040
133	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts`, `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`
134	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
135	
136	`member` is the `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum for `project:create`, `project:update`,
137	`issue:create`, `issue:update`, `issue:assign`, `issue:archive`, `comment:create` and
138	`comment:update`. This is the working-contributor role: enough to do the day-to-day job of
139	running a project and triaging issues, without the organizational authority of `admin`
140	(inviting people, archiving projects, deleting issues).
141	
142	**Acceptance criteria**
143	
144	1. A `member` can call `createIssueAction`, `createProjectAction` and
145	   `createCommentAction` successfully against a resource in their own org.
146	2. A `member` calling `deleteIssueAction`-equivalent flows (which require `admin`) is
147	   denied.
148	3. A `member`'s issue update to a field they are not the author or assignee of still
149	   succeeds, because `issue:update`'s matrix minimum is already `member`, independent of
150	   the ownership escalation in `REQ-026`.
151	
152	### REQ-024 — Admins manage membership, flags and archiving
153	
154	- **Priority:** must
155	- **Status:** implemented

---
title: Membership and roles requirements
id: REQ-MEMBERSHIP
status: approved
owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
last_updated: 2026-05-11
related: [REQ-001, REQ-006, ADR-003, DES-011]
---

## Scope

This document defines how a user becomes a member of an organization, what the four roles
mean, how invitations work end to end, and the invariants that keep the last-owner rule and
authored-content ownership consistent under role changes and removals. It does not define
the tenant boundary itself (`organizations.md`) or what each permission action actually
gates on individual resources like issues and comments (`issues.md`,
`comments-and-mentions.md`), though the ownership-escalation mechanic is defined here because
it is a property of roles, not of any one resource.

## Context

Membership is a join between a global `User` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`,
the one repository that is not tenant-scoped) and an `Organization`, represented as a
`Member` row with a `role`. `src/server/services/member-service.ts` owns role changes and
removal; `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` owns the invite-and-accept lifecycle
that produces new members. Both call into `src/lib/permissions.ts`, which is the single
authorization entry point (`ADR-003`): `can()`, `assertCan()`, `explain()` and `canAll()`
all read from one `ROLE_MATRIX` table keyed by `PermissionAction`.

The four roles — `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer` — form a strict total order captured
in `ROLE_RANK` (`src/types/member.ts`). `ROLE_MATRIX` records, for every action, the minimum
role required, and `hasRoleAtLeast` is the comparison every "at least this role" check
reduces to. The decision order documented in `permissions.ts` runs cross-tenant guard,
platform-staff bypass, role matrix, then ownership escalation — so a `member` who is not
the assignee of an issue is denied `issue:update` by the matrix, but the same `member` who
authored that issue is granted it by the escalation step that runs after the matrix would
otherwise deny.

Invitations are their own short-lived entity (`src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts`),
keyed by a hash of the invite token rather than the plaintext token, so the unauthenticated
accept page (`src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`) never has to trust a value it cannot
verify against the database. `invitation-service.ts` checks the seat quota
(`wouldExceedLimit`) and the `member:invite` rate-limit bucket before it mints a token,
which is why an org near its seat limit gets `plan_limit_exceeded` before Taskflow ever
writes a pending invitation row it would have to clean up later.

## Open questions

1. `REQ-026`'s ownership escalation list (`issue:update`, `issue:archive`,
   `comment:update`, `comment:delete`, `notification:manage`) is fixed in `permissions.ts`;
   whether project leads (`REQ-049`) should get an analogous escalation for
   `project:update` is an open product question, not yet a requirement.
2. `REQ-027`'s platform-staff bypass has no requirement here describing how staff status is
   granted or revoked — that lives outside this corpus's scope (an internal admin tool).
3. `REQ-032` checks seats at invite time; whether an accepted invitation should re-check the
   seat quota at acceptance time (a window where the quota could have been exhausted by a
   concurrent invite) is unresolved — see the note under `REQ-030`.

### REQ-020 — Four roles form a strict rank order

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-003, REQ-021, DES-011
- **Implemented by:** `src/types/member.ts` — `ROLE_RANK`, `hasRoleAtLeast`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/schemas/member.schema.test.ts`

`ROLE_RANK` in `src/types/member.ts` orders the four roles `owner > admin > member >
viewer`, and every "minimum role" check in the product — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `hasRoleAtLeast`,
the last-owner guard — is expressed against this single ordering rather than an ad hoc set
of role comparisons scattered per feature. There is no fifth role and no per-organization
custom role; Taskflow deliberately does not offer role customization, trading flexibility
for a permission surface simple enough to reason about in one file.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `ROLE_RANK` assigns a strictly increasing numeric rank to `viewer < member < admin <
   owner`.
2. Every comparison of "is this role at least that role" in the codebase goes through
   `hasRoleAtLeast`, not a hand-rolled string comparison.
3. Role values outside the four are rejected at the schema layer (`src/schemas/role.ts`).

### REQ-021 — Role rank determines the default permission decision

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-020, ADR-003, REQ-027

For any `PermissionAction`, `ROLE_MATRIX` declares a minimum role; `can()` compares the
actor's role rank against that minimum after the cross-tenant and platform-staff checks have
already passed. This is the `granted_by_role` / `denied_by_role` branch of `explain()`'s
decision reasons, and it is the default path — most calls to `can()` in the app resolve here
without ever reaching the ownership-escalation step.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `can(actor, action)` returns `true` whenever `actor.role` rank is greater than or equal
   to the action's `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum.
2. `explain()` reports `granted_by_role` or `denied_by_role` for every action not covered
   by an escalation.
3. `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` sweeps every action against every role.

**Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

### REQ-022 — Viewers have read-only access across the product

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-020, REQ-181, REQ-224
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/components/domain/permission/permission-gate.tsx`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`, `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`

`viewer` is the minimum role for every `*:read` action in `ROLE_MATRIX` —
`org:read`, `member:read`, `project:read`, `issue:read`, `comment:read`,
`notification:read` — and the minimum role for no mutating action at all. A viewer can open
every screen a member can, but every button that would write is hidden by
`PermissionGate` (see `tests/components/permission-gate.test.tsx`) and, more importantly,
would be denied server-side even if a viewer forged the request.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No `*:create`, `*:update`, `*:delete`, `*:archive` or `*:manage_*` action's `ROLE_MATRIX`
   minimum is `viewer`.
2. Every `*:read` action's minimum is `viewer` or lower (there is no lower role).
3. A viewer's forged Server Action call is denied server-side regardless of what the client
   rendered.

### REQ-023 — Members may create and edit issues, projects and comments

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-060, REQ-090, REQ-040
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts`, `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`member` is the `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum for `project:create`, `project:update`,
`issue:create`, `issue:update`, `issue:assign`, `issue:archive`, `comment:create` and
`comment:update`. This is the working-contributor role: enough to do the day-to-day job of
running a project and triaging issues, without the organizational authority of `admin`
(inviting people, archiving projects, deleting issues).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `member` can call `createIssueAction`, `createProjectAction` and
   `createCommentAction` successfully against a resource in their own org.
2. A `member` calling `deleteIssueAction`-equivalent flows (which require `admin`) is
   denied.
3. A `member`'s issue update to a field they are not the author or assignee of still
   succeeds, because `issue:update`'s matrix minimum is already `member`, independent of
   the ownership escalation in `REQ-026`.

### REQ-024 — Admins manage membership, flags and archiving

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-028, REQ-192, REQ-045
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`admin` is the `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum for `member:invite`, `member:update_role`,
`member:remove`, `org:manage_flags`, `org:update`, `project:archive`, `issue:delete`,
`comment:delete`, `activity:export` and `webhook:manage`. Admins run the organizational side
of the product — who's in it, what's turned on, what gets archived — everything short of
the two owner-only actions (`org:delete`, `org:manage_billing`).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An `admin` can invite a member, toggle a feature flag and archive a project in one
   session without hitting a permission wall.
2. An `admin` cannot change the plan or delete the organization (`REQ-025`).
3. Every action listed above has `admin` as its exact `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum, not `owner`.

### REQ-025 — Owners alone may delete the organization or change billing

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-007, REQ-140, DES-021
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`, `src/actions/billing/update-seats.ts`, `src/actions/billing/cancel-subscription.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`org:delete` and `org:manage_billing` are the only two actions whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum
is `owner`. Every billing action — `changePlanAction`, `updateSeatsAction`,
`cancelSubscriptionAction` — is gated on `org:manage_billing`, so an `admin` who can do
almost everything else in settings still cannot see or press the change-plan button;
`billing/page.tsx` renders it behind the same `can()` check the server enforces.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `can(actor, 'org:manage_billing')` is `false` for every role below `owner`.
2. `changePlanAction` called by an `admin` returns a `forbidden` `ActionResult`, not a
   silently ignored no-op.
3. The billing settings page hides mutating controls from non-owners but still renders the
   current plan read-only, since `org:read` remains available to everyone.

### REQ-026 — Authors may edit their own issues and comments regardless of rank

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-072, REQ-097, ADR-003

1	---
2	title: Comments and mentions requirements
3	id: REQ-COMMENTS
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-04-27
7	related: [REQ-090, REQ-060, REQ-112, DES-110]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for issue comments: creation, Markdown handling,
13	mention parsing and its resolution to organization members, rate limiting, editing and soft
14	delete, and thread ordering. It does not define the notification behavior a mention
15	triggers — that belongs to `notifications-and-digests.md` — though `REQ-095` and `REQ-112`
16	are the seam between the two documents and are cross-referenced in both places.
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	A comment belongs to exactly one issue and, through it, one organization; the schema is
21	`src/server/db/schema/comments.ts`, the repository is
22	`src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts`, and the business rules live in
23	`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`. Comments are soft deleted (`archiveComment`) rather
24	than removed, consistent with `ADR-004`, which is what lets a deleted comment keep its
25	position in a thread — later comments that quote or reply to it still make sense in context
26	even after the original is gone.
27	
28	Comment bodies are Markdown, but a restricted subset: `src/lib/markdown.ts#renderMarkdown`
29	implements a small renderer rather than pulling in a general-purpose Markdown library, which
30	bounds what a comment can actually do to the surface the product wants to support (bold,
31	italic, links, code spans and fences, lists) rather than the full CommonMark surface,
32	including anything that would need sanitization against arbitrary HTML.
33	
34	Mentions are parsed from the comment body at write time by `src/lib/mentions.ts`:
35	`extractMentions` finds `@handle`-shaped tokens, and `resolveMentions` maps them against the
36	organization's member list to produce the `UserId`s the comment actually mentions — a
37	syntactic `@handle` that does not match any member of the same org resolves to nothing,
38	consistent with `REQ-094`. Because comment bodies contain code spans and fences that
39	routinely include `@` characters (email examples, npm scope references), `extractMentions`
40	excludes text inside backticks and fenced code blocks before it looks for mention syntax —
41	this is `REQ-093`, and it is the one part of mention parsing that most needs a real
42	Markdown-aware pass rather than a regex over raw text, which is exactly why it is
43	implemented against the same tokenizer `renderMarkdown` uses rather than as an independent
44	string search.
45	
46	Commenting is the one write in the product that is open to every role: `comment:create`
47	carries a `viewer` minimum in `ROLE_MATRIX`, so a read-only collaborator brought into an
48	organization to review work can still reply on a thread without being promoted to `member`.
49	This was a deliberate product call — the alternative, promoting reviewers to `member` just
50	so they could answer a question, handed them project and issue write access nobody wanted
51	them to have.
52	
53	Comment creation goes through the `comment:create` rate-limit bucket
54	(`consumeRateLimit(orgId, 'comment:create', ...)`, capacity 60, refill 20/minute) before the
55	write happens, protecting the mention fan-out and the search index from a burst of automated
56	or accidental rapid-fire comments overwhelming downstream consumers in one moment.
57	
58	Comment edits are not versioned: `updateComment` overwrites the stored body in place, so
59	there is no edit history a reader can inspect the way some issue-tracking products expose a
60	"show edit history" link. This is a deliberate simplicity trade-off — the team weighed a
61	comment-revision table early in the design and decided the audit trail's activity row
62	(`REQ-034`'s sibling for comments) was sufficient evidence of "this was edited and by whom
63	and when," without the storage and query cost of keeping every prior body around indefinitely.
64	
65	## Open questions
66	
67	1. `REQ-091`'s restricted Markdown subset has no requirement enumerating exactly which
68	   syntax is supported beyond what `renderMarkdown`'s implementation happens to accept —
69	   the requirements corpus intentionally treats this as an implementation detail rather than
70	   a frozen spec, which risks silent behavior drift across renderer changes.
71	2. `REQ-102` re-parses mentions on edit, but there is no requirement describing whether a
72	   removed mention should also remove or mark stale any notification already sent for it —
73	   see the related gap noted in `notifications-and-digests.md`.
74	3. Whether comment rate limiting (`REQ-096`) should scale with plan the way
75	   `apiRequestsPerHour` does, rather than using one fixed bucket for every plan, is
76	   unresolved.
77	
78	### REQ-090 — Comments belong to an issue and an organization
79	
80	- **Priority:** must
81	- **Status:** implemented
82	- **Related:** REQ-060, REQ-010, DES-110
83	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts` — `findCommentById`, `listComments`, `listThread`
84	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/comment-repository.test.ts`
85	
86	`comments` carries both `org_id` and `issue_id`; there is no organization-level or
87	project-level comment independent of a specific issue. `findCommentById(orgId, commentId)`
88	enforces the org scope on every lookup, and `listComments`/`listThread` additionally require
89	the `issueId` the caller is viewing.
90	
91	**Acceptance criteria**
92	
93	1. `insertComment` requires a valid, existing `issueId` within the same `orgId`.
94	2. A comment cannot be fetched across organizations even by a correct `commentId` guess.
95	3. Deleting the parent issue does not orphan comments into a queryable "issue-less" state —
96	   they are governed by the same archive cascade path as the issue itself.
97	
98	### REQ-091 — Comment bodies are Markdown with a restricted subset
99	
100	- **Priority:** must
101	- **Status:** implemented
102	- **Related:** REQ-092, DES-100
103	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/markdown.ts` — `renderMarkdown`, `stripMarkdown`, `excerpt`
104	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/markdown.test.ts`
105	
106	`renderMarkdown` in `src/lib/markdown.ts` renders the subset the product supports; raw HTML
107	in a comment body is not passed through, and `stripMarkdown`/`excerpt` provide plain-text
108	projections used by notification previews and search snippets so those surfaces never leak
109	unrendered Markdown syntax to a reader.
110	
111	**Acceptance criteria**
112	
113	1. A comment body is stored as raw Markdown text, not pre-rendered HTML.
114	2. `renderMarkdown` output never includes an unescaped `<script>` or other raw HTML tag from
115	   the input.
116	3. `excerpt` truncates on a word boundary and does not cut a Markdown link or code span in
117	   half in a way that would break rendering of the truncated excerpt.
118	
119	### REQ-092 — Mentions are parsed from the comment body at write time
120	
121	- **Priority:** must
122	- **Status:** implemented
123	- **Related:** REQ-095, REQ-112, DES-110
124	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/mentions.ts` — `extractMentions`, `src/server/services/comment-service.ts` — `createComment`, `updateComment`
125	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/mentions.test.ts`
126	
127	`extractMentions(body)` runs during `createComment` and `updateComment`, before the write
128	completes, so the set of mentioned users is computed once and stored as part of what
129	`comment.created`/the edit path reports — mentions are not re-derived lazily by a reader
130	opening the comment later, keeping notification fan-out deterministic and independent of
131	when someone happens to view the thread.
132	
133	**Acceptance criteria**
134	
135	1. `extractMentions` returns the raw `@handle` tokens found in the body, in order of first
136	   occurrence.
137	2. Mention extraction happens synchronously within `createComment`, not as a deferred job.
138	3. A comment with no `@` tokens produces an empty mention set, not an error.
139	
140	### REQ-093 — Mentions inside code spans and fences are not mentions
141	
142	- **Priority:** must
143	- **Status:** implemented
144	- **Related:** REQ-092, REQ-091
145	
146	`extractMentions` excludes any `@handle`-shaped text that falls inside inline code
147	(single backticks) or a fenced code block (triple backticks), so a comment discussing an
148	`@scope/package` npm reference or quoting an email header does not spuriously notify a
149	member whose handle happens to match.

routinely include `@` characters (email examples, npm scope references), `extractMentions`
excludes text inside backticks and fenced code blocks before it looks for mention syntax —
this is `REQ-093`, and it is the one part of mention parsing that most needs a real
Markdown-aware pass rather than a regex over raw text, which is exactly why it is
implemented against the same tokenizer `renderMarkdown` uses rather than as an independent
string search.

Commenting is the one write in the product that is open to every role: `comment:create`
carries a `viewer` minimum in `ROLE_MATRIX`, so a read-only collaborator brought into an
organization to review work can still reply on a thread without being promoted to `member`.
This was a deliberate product call — the alternative, promoting reviewers to `member` just
so they could answer a question, handed them project and issue write access nobody wanted
them to have.

Comment creation goes through the `comment:create` rate-limit bucket
(`consumeRateLimit(orgId, 'comment:create', ...)`, capacity 60, refill 20/minute) before the
write happens, protecting the mention fan-out and the search index from a burst of automated
or accidental rapid-fire comments overwhelming downstream consumers in one moment.

Comment edits are not versioned: `updateComment` overwrites the stored body in place, so
there is no edit history a reader can inspect the way some issue-tracking products expose a
"show edit history" link. This is a deliberate simplicity trade-off — the team weighed a
comment-revision table early in the design and decided the audit trail's activity row
(`REQ-034`'s sibling for comments) was sufficient evidence of "this was edited and by whom
and when," without the storage and query cost of keeping every prior body around indefinitely.

## Open questions

1. `REQ-091`'s restricted Markdown subset has no requirement enumerating exactly which
   syntax is supported beyond what `renderMarkdown`'s implementation happens to accept —
   the requirements corpus intentionally treats this as an implementation detail rather than
   a frozen spec, which risks silent behavior drift across renderer changes.
2. `REQ-102` re-parses mentions on edit, but there is no requirement describing whether a
   removed mention should also remove or mark stale any notification already sent for it —
   see the related gap noted in `notifications-and-digests.md`.
3. Whether comment rate limiting (`REQ-096`) should scale with plan the way
   `apiRequestsPerHour` does, rather than using one fixed bucket for every plan, is
   unresolved.

### REQ-090 — Comments belong to an issue and an organization

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-060, REQ-010, DES-110
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts` — `findCommentById`, `listComments`, `listThread`
- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/comment-repository.test.ts`

`comments` carries both `org_id` and `issue_id`; there is no organization-level or
project-level comment independent of a specific issue. `findCommentById(orgId, commentId)`
enforces the org scope on every lookup, and `listComments`/`listThread` additionally require
the `issueId` the caller is viewing.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `insertComment` requires a valid, existing `issueId` within the same `orgId`.
2. A comment cannot be fetched across organizations even by a correct `commentId` guess.
3. Deleting the parent issue does not orphan comments into a queryable "issue-less" state —
   they are governed by the same archive cascade path as the issue itself.

### REQ-091 — Comment bodies are Markdown with a restricted subset

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-092, DES-100
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/markdown.ts` — `renderMarkdown`, `stripMarkdown`, `excerpt`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/markdown.test.ts`

`renderMarkdown` in `src/lib/markdown.ts` renders the subset the product supports; raw HTML
in a comment body is not passed through, and `stripMarkdown`/`excerpt` provide plain-text
projections used by notification previews and search snippets so those surfaces never leak
unrendered Markdown syntax to a reader.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A comment body is stored as raw Markdown text, not pre-rendered HTML.
2. `renderMarkdown` output never includes an unescaped `<script>` or other raw HTML tag from
   the input.
3. `excerpt` truncates on a word boundary and does not cut a Markdown link or code span in
   half in a way that would break rendering of the truncated excerpt.

### REQ-092 — Mentions are parsed from the comment body at write time

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-095, REQ-112, DES-110
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/mentions.ts` — `extractMentions`, `src/server/services/comment-service.ts` — `createComment`, `updateComment`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/mentions.test.ts`

`extractMentions(body)` runs during `createComment` and `updateComment`, before the write
completes, so the set of mentioned users is computed once and stored as part of what
`comment.created`/the edit path reports — mentions are not re-derived lazily by a reader
opening the comment later, keeping notification fan-out deterministic and independent of
when someone happens to view the thread.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `extractMentions` returns the raw `@handle` tokens found in the body, in order of first
   occurrence.
2. Mention extraction happens synchronously within `createComment`, not as a deferred job.
3. A comment with no `@` tokens produces an empty mention set, not an error.

### REQ-093 — Mentions inside code spans and fences are not mentions

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-092, REQ-091

`extractMentions` excludes any `@handle`-shaped text that falls inside inline code
(single backticks) or a fenced code block (triple backticks), so a comment discussing an
`@scope/package` npm reference or quoting an email header does not spuriously notify a
member whose handle happens to match.
